A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Super Experts study and retain matching core methods and experiments. All pages, including appendices, were readable; text extraction and visual inspection supported comparison of equations, tables, and figures.

before.justification: v1 reports original expert-pruning evaluations, activation analyses, attention-sink measurements, and qualitative generation results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds layer-controlled pruning comparisons, router analyses, weight-pruning cases, and sparse-autoencoder findings.

M1.justification: The main SE identification rule remains unchanged between v1 Equation 8 and v2 Equation 6. Appendix H adds an auxiliary methodology involving super-weight interventions, a trained sparse autoencoder, and decoder-weight-based feature selection. The new description of dynamic pruning does not establish that the original pruning procedure changed.

E1.justification: The established text benchmark and cross-domain profiling coverage is retained. v2 Tables 11-12 add a limited visual-question-answering extension using LLaVA-V1.5-7B on two images. Additional dense-model analyses largely reuse existing text domains and datasets.

E2.justification: v2 Tables 3-5 add layer-controlled random pruning alongside the original model and global random-pruning comparators. This supplies a new comparator within the existing experiments. Discussed methods such as M-SMoE, NAEE, and MC remain related work rather than evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The evaluation design expands through pruning controls restricted to SE-containing layers, targeted weight-pruning experiments, and SAE feature probes. New settings include Llama-2-7B attention diagnostics on MMLU and SAE training on Llama-3.2-1B layer-1 FFN activations from C4. These are additional protocols; the retained benchmark settings do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: v2 adds substantial mechanistic analyses: sink-versus-nonsink router distributions across datasets, QKV suppression and cosine-similarity diagnostics, super-weight pruning across model types, and SAE feature interpretation. The layer-controlled comparisons also test whether SE importance merely reflects layer location. v1's outlier-expert, cross-domain, and generation analyses largely survive in v2 Appendices C-E.

E5.justification: Both versions state that Table 3 random-pruning results average five runs. v2 adds comparison rows without introducing a different uncertainty-reporting practice, additional seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: v2 adds LC-random results, including average scores of 70.21 for non-thinking Qwen3 and 75.51 for DeepSeek-R1, plus router, weight-pruning, and SAE findings. Existing task scores are largely retained. Numerical corrections include DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat's SE proportion from 0.22% to 0.11% and global-random average drop rates from 0.32% to 0.15% and 0.06% in Tables 4 and 5, respectively.

T1.justification: v2 Appendix H introduces mathematical definitions of the SAE reconstruction and weighted sparsity losses in Equations 8-9. The SE threshold and attention-sink decay definitions retain their mathematical content. No new theorem or proof is supplied.

C1.justification: v1 centers its contributions on discovering SEs, establishing their importance, and connecting their pruning to attention-sink disruption. v2 broadens the abstract and contribution statements to identify SEs as the primary source of systematic outliers and position the findings as a foundation for expert-balanced pretraining as well as compression.

C2.justification: v2 develops explanations involving preferential sink-token routing, weight outliers, progressive activation formation, and QKV behavior. Appendix H additionally interprets end-of-text-associated SAE features as explaining repetitive generation and assigns SEs a role in termination control. This interpretation extends beyond v1's observation of reasoning collapse and relies partly on extrapolation from a dense model.

D1.justification: v2 adds profiling pseudocode, super-weight coordinates, SAE training and feature-selection details, and explicit descriptions of dynamic skipping and attention-sink calibration. It also revises DeepSeek-V2-Lite SE layer labels from 2/3 to 3/4 without establishing a different experimental run. The repository link remains unchanged, and important SAE hyperparameter values remain unspecified.

R1.justification: New Appendix B substantially develops positioning within systematic-outlier research, discussing no-op attention behavior and outlier mitigation through gated or modified attention. New references include KVSink, gated-attention work, Softpick, and SAE research. This expands the scientific positioning beyond the earlier emphasis on expert-level compression.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, and Section 5 undergo substantial rewriting. The preliminaries are shortened, localization subsections are reorganized, and the appendix structure expands around retained material. Ethics, reproducibility, and language-model-use statements are also added.

P2.justification: The document switches from two-column to single-column layout, restructures tables, and rearranges Figure 5's model pairs. v2 adds router plots, mechanism diagrams, SAE visualizations, weight-pruning tables, and an algorithm display. Existing appendix heatmaps are retained under new numbering, while the attention-map display drops the layer-15 pair.

improvement.justification: The added layer-controlled comparisons strengthen attribution of performance collapse specifically to SEs, and the router and weight-level analyses provide useful additional evidence. However, the termination explanation remains indirect, and reproducibility gains are limited by missing SAE settings and a new inconsistency: Algorithm 1 constructs its percentile pool within selected layers, whereas Section 3.2.1 defines it across the entire model. These tradeoffs support a limited net improvement rather than a clear substantial gain.
